summary.text: Torres grew up in public housing in the Bronx and began his career as a staffer to a City Council member. He was elected to the New York City Council in 2013 at age 25 and to Congress in 2020, and has represented NY-15 since January 2021. He sits on the House Financial Services Committee and the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with the Chinese Communist Party, and has sponsored legislation on housing, immigration-detention oversight, and campaign-finance transparency.

paragraphs.text: Ritchie Torres was born in the Bronx on March 12, 1988.
According to his official biography, his mother raised him, his twin brother, and his sister in a public-housing project, working minimum-wage jobs.
He graduated from Herbert H. Lehman High School in the Bronx in 2006 and attended New York University from 2006 to 2007.
Before seeking office he worked on the staff of Bronx City Council Member Jimmy Vacca and as a community organizer.

Torres was elected to the New York City Council in 2013 at age 25, becoming the city's youngest elected official and, per his official biography, the first openly LGBTQ+ person elected to office in the Bronx.
He represented District 15 until his election to Congress.

On the Council he chaired the committee overseeing the New York City Housing Authority (NYCHA), where, according to his official biography, he held the first committee hearing ever in public housing, and he served as a delegate to the 2016 Democratic National Convention.
Torres was elected to the U.S. House in 2020 to succeed Rep. José Serrano and took office in January 2021.
In the 117th Congress he served on the Financial Services and Homeland Security Committees.

In the 119th Congress he serves on Financial Services, with subcommittee seats on Digital Assets, Financial Technology, and Artificial Intelligence; Housing and Insurance; and National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions, and on the Select Committee on Strategic Competition with the Chinese Communist Party.
